title: Acute Cholecystitis Versus Biliary Colic: Key Differences
subject: Surgery
preview: Biliary colic typically produces episodic pain from transient cystic duct obstruction without persistent inflammation.
quickRevision: Biliary colic typically produces episodic pain from transient cystic duct obstruction without persistent inflammation.
Ultrasound may show gallstones, gallbladder wall changes and pericholecystic findings.
Cholangitis must be considered when biliary symptoms are accompanied by systemic infection and cholestasis.

sections.title: Clinical syndrome and red flags
points: Biliary colic typically produces episodic pain from transient cystic duct obstruction without persistent inflammation.
Acute cholecystitis more often involves sustained pain, localized tenderness, and inflammatory features.

sections.title: Differentiate and manage
points: Ultrasound may show gallstones, gallbladder wall changes and pericholecystic findings.
Cholangitis must be considered when biliary symptoms are accompanied by systemic infection and cholestasis.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Do not use presence of gallstones alone to conclude that every abdominal pain episode is acute cholecystitis.

quiz.question: Which feature favors acute cholecystitis over uncomplicated biliary colic?
quiz.explanation: Persistent RUQ pain with inflammation. Biliary colic typically produces episodic pain from transient cystic duct obstruction without persistent inflammation.
